1.title: Short Title, Commencement and Application
1.text: Establishes the formal title, territorial jurisdiction, and effective date of the BNS, including its application to offences within and beyond India.

2.title: Definitions
2.text: Provides modern and inclusive definitions relevant for contemporary legal application, such as including transgender under gender and electronic records under document.

3.title: General Explanations
3.text: Provides general principles for interpreting the provisions of the Sanhita, including the application of general exceptions, possession, and joint liability.

4.title: Punishments
4.text: Specifies the range of punishments available under the Sanhita, including modern additions like community service, applicable to various offences.

5.title: Commutation of Sentence
5.text: Provides the framework for commutation of sentences by the appropriate government authority, referencing procedural guidelines in the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.

6.title: Fractions of Terms of Punishment
6.text: Establishes a standard for computing imprisonment for life as equivalent to 20 years for the purpose of calculating fractional terms, unless specified otherwise.

7.title: Sentence May Be (In Certain Cases of Imprisonment) Wholly or Partly Rigorous or Simple
7.text: Grants courts discretion to determine whether imprisonment is rigorous, simple, or a combination of both, depending on the case.

8.title: Amount of Fine, Liability in Default of Payment of Fine, etc.
8.text: Regulates the imposition of fines, including limits, default imprisonment terms, and compensation to victims, ensuring fines are reasonable and enforceable.

9.title: Limit of Punishment of Offence Made Up of Several Offences
9.text: Prevents excessive punishment when an offence comprises multiple parts or falls under multiple definitions, limiting punishment to the most severe applicable penalty.

10.title: Punishment of Person Guilty of One of Several Offences, the Judgment Stating That It Is Doubtful of Which
10.text: Ensures that when guilt is established for one of multiple offences but the specific offence is unclear, the offender receives the least severe punishment among the possible offences.

11.title: Solitary Confinement
11.text: Allows courts to impose solitary confinement as part of rigorous imprisonment, with limits based on the total imprisonment term to ensure proportionality.

12.title: Limit of Solitary Confinement
12.text: Sets strict limits on the duration and frequency of solitary confinement to prevent excessive use, ensuring humane treatment during punishment.

13.title: Enhanced Punishment for Certain Offences After Previous Conviction
13.text: Provides for enhanced punishment for repeat offenders convicted of serious offences under specific chapters, aiming to deter recidivism.

14.title: Act Done by a Person Bound, or by Mistake of Fact Believing Himself Bound, by Law
14.text: Exempts acts done under a legal obligation or in good faith belief of such obligation due to a mistake of fact, but not a mistake of law.

15.title: Act of Judge When Acting Judicially
15.text: Protects judges from liability for acts performed in their judicial capacity, provided they act in good faith within their perceived legal authority.

16.title: Act Done Pursuant to the Judgment or Order of Court
16.text: Exempts acts done under a court's judgment or order, even if the court lacked jurisdiction, as long as the person acted in good faith believing the court had authority.

17.title: Act Done by a Person Justified, or by Mistake of Fact Believing Himself, Justified, by Law
17.text: Protects individuals acting under legal justification or in good faith belief of such justification due to a mistake of fact, not law.

18.title: Accident in Doing a Lawful Act
18.text: Exempts accidental acts causing harm during lawful activities, provided they are performed with due care and without criminal intent.

19.title: Act Likely to Cause Harm, but Done Without Criminal Intent, and to Prevent Other Harm
19.text: Exempts acts done in good faith to prevent greater harm, without criminal intent, even if they risk causing harm, subject to the imminence and necessity of the situation.

20.title: Act of a Child Under Seven Years of Age
20.text: Grants absolute immunity from criminal liability to children under seven, recognizing their lack of capacity to form criminal intent.

21.title: Act of a Child Above Seven and Under Twelve of Immature Understanding
21.text: Provides conditional immunity to children aged seven to twelve, exempting them if they lack sufficient maturity to understand their actions' consequences.

22.title: Act of a Person of Unsound Mind
22.text: Exempts individuals with mental incapacity from liability if they cannot understand the nature or wrongfulness of their actions due to unsoundness of mind.

23.title: Act of a Person Incapable of Judgment by Reason of Intoxication Caused Against His Will
23.text: Exempts acts done under involuntary intoxication if the person was unable to understand the nature or wrongfulness of their actions, provided the intoxication was not self-induced.

24.title: Offence Requiring a Particular Intent or Knowledge Committed by One Who Is Intoxicated
24.text: Holds voluntarily intoxicated individuals liable for offences requiring specific intent or knowledge, assuming they had the same knowledge as if sober, unless intoxication was involuntary.

25.title: Act Not Intended and Not Known to Be Likely to Cause Death or Grievous Hurt, Done by Consent
25.text: Exempts harm caused with consent by adults, provided the act was not intended or known to be likely to cause death or grievous hurt, recognizing consensual risk-taking.

26.title: Act Not Intended to Cause Death, Done by Consent in Good Faith for Person’s Benefit
26.text: Exempts harm caused in good faith for a person’s benefit with their consent, such as in medical procedures, provided there was no intent to cause death.

27.title: Act Done in Good Faith for Benefit of Child or Person of Unsound Mind, by or by Consent of Guardian
27.text: Allows acts done in good faith for the benefit of children under twelve or persons of unsound mind with guardian consent, with strict limitations to prevent intentional or reckless harm.

28.title: Consent Known to Be Given Under Fear or Misconception
28.text: Invalidates consent given under fear, misconception, or by those incapable of understanding due to age, unsound mind, or intoxication, ensuring consent is free and informed.

29.title: Exclusion of Acts Which Are Offences Independently of Harm Caused
29.text: Clarifies that consent-based exceptions do not apply to acts that are offences regardless of the harm caused, such as causing miscarriage outside specific circumstances.

30.title: Act Done in Good Faith for Benefit of a Person Without Consent
30.text: Permits acts done in good faith for a person’s benefit without consent in urgent situations where consent is impossible, with limitations to prevent intentional or reckless harm.

31.title: Communication Made in Good Faith
31.text: Exempts good-faith communications made for a person’s benefit, even if they cause harm, such as a doctor’s prognosis causing emotional distress.

32.title: Act to Which a Person Is Compelled by Threats
32.text: Exempts acts done under immediate threat of death, except for murder or certain offences against the State, provided the person did not voluntarily expose themselves to such threats.

33.title: Act Causing Slight Harm
33.text: Exempts acts causing minimal harm that a reasonable person would not consider significant enough to warrant complaint, avoiding unnecessary criminalization of trivial acts.

34.title: Things Done in Private Defence
34.text: Grants a general exemption for acts done in lawful self-defence or defence of property, subject to limitations outlined in subsequent sections.

35.title: Right of Private Defence of Body and of Property
35.text: Establishes the right to defend one’s body or property, or that of others, against specific offences, subject to proportionality and necessity constraints.

36.title: Right of Private Defence Against the Act of a Person of Unsound Mind, etc.
36.text: Extends the right of private defence to acts by individuals who are not criminally liable due to youth, mental incapacity, or misconception, treating the act as if it were an offence.

37.title: Acts Against Which There Is No Right of Private Defence
37.text: Limits the right of private defence against acts by public servants or under their direction, and when public authorities can be accessed, emphasizing proportionality in defensive actions.

38.title: When Right of Private Defence of Body Extends to Causing Death
38.text: Permits causing death in defence of the body against serious assaults, such as those threatening death, grievous hurt, rape, or kidnapping, subject to proportionality and necessity constraints.

39.title: When Such Right Extends to Causing Any Harm Other Than Death
39.text: Allows causing harm short of death in defence of the body against less severe assaults, subject to proportionality and necessity constraints.

40.title: Commencement and Continuance of Right of Private Defence of Body
40.text: Defines the timing of the right of private defence of the body, starting when there is reasonable apprehension of danger and continuing until the threat subsides.

41.title: When Right of Private Defence of Property Extends to Causing Death
41.text: Permits causing death in defence of property against specific serious offences like robbery or house-breaking by night, subject to proportionality and necessity constraints.

42.title: When Such Right Extends to Causing Any Harm Other Than Death
42.text: Allows causing harm short of death in defence of property against less severe offences like theft or criminal trespass, subject to proportionality and necessity constraints.

43.title: Commencement and continuance of right of private defence of property.

44.title: Right of Private Defence Against Deadly Assault When There Is Risk of Harm to Innocent Person
44.text: Allows the exercise of private defence against a deadly assault even if it risks harming innocent persons, recognizing the necessity of self-preservation in extreme circumstances.

45.title: Abetment of a Thing
45.text: Defines abetment as instigating, conspiring, or aiding the commission of an act, establishing liability for facilitating offences.
45.chapter: Chapter IV: Of Abetment, Criminal Conspiracy and Attempt

46.title: Abettor
46.text: Clarifies who qualifies as an abettor, emphasizing that abetment applies even if the offence is not completed or the person abetted lacks criminal capacity or intent.
46.chapter: Chapter IV: Of Abetment, Criminal Conspiracy and Attempt

47.title: Abetment in India of Offences Outside India
47.text: Extends liability for abetment to acts instigated in India for offences committed abroad, treating them as if committed in India.
47.chapter: Chapter IV: Of Abetment, Criminal Conspiracy and Attempt

48.title: Abetment Outside India for Offence in India
48.text: Holds individuals liable for abetting offences in India from abroad, ensuring jurisdiction over cross-border instigation.
48.chapter: Chapter IV: Of Abetment, Criminal Conspiracy and Attempt

49.title: Punishment of Abetment if the Act Abetted Is Committed in Consequence and Where No Express Provision Is Made for Its Punishment
49.text: Specifies that abettors are liable for the same punishment as the principal offender if the abetted act is committed, absent specific provisions.
49.chapter: Chapter IV: Of Abetment, Criminal Conspiracy and Attempt

50.title: Punishment of Abetment if Person Abetted Does Act With Different Intention From That of Abettor
50.text: Ensures abettors are punished based on the intended offence, even if the person abetted acts with a different intent, limiting liability to the abettor’s purpose.
50.chapter: Chapter IV: Of Abetment, Criminal Conspiracy and Attempt

51.title: Liability of Abettor When One Act Abetted and Different Act Done
51.text: Holds abettors liable for unintended acts done as probable consequences of their abetment, ensuring accountability for foreseeable outcomes.
51.chapter: Chapter IV: Of Abetment, Criminal Conspiracy and Attempt

52.title: Abettor When Liable to Cumulative Punishment for Act Abetted and for Act Done
52.text: Allows cumulative punishment for abettors when the act done constitutes a distinct offence in addition to the abetted act, ensuring liability for all offences committed.
52.chapter: Chapter IV: Of Abetment, Criminal Conspiracy and Attempt

53.title: Liability of Abettor for an Effect Caused by the Act Abetted Different From That Intended by the Abettor
53.text: Holds abettors liable for unintended effects of the abetted act if they knew such effects were likely, ensuring accountability for foreseeable consequences.
53.chapter: Chapter IV: Of Abetment, Criminal Conspiracy and Attempt

54.title: Abettor Present When Offence Is Committed
54.text: Treats abettors present at the commission of the abetted offence as principal offenders, enhancing their liability for direct involvement.
54.chapter: Chapter IV: Of Abetment, Criminal Conspiracy and Attempt

55.title: Abetment of Offence Punishable With Death or Imprisonment for Life if Offence Not Committed
55.text: Provides punishment for abetting serious offences like those punishable with death or life imprisonment, even if the offence is not committed, to deter instigation.
55.chapter: Chapter IV: Of Abetment, Criminal Conspiracy and Attempt

56.title: Abetment of Offence Punishable With Imprisonment if Offence Be Not Committed
56.text: Punishes abetment of offences punishable with imprisonment, even if uncommitted, with a reduced term to deter instigation while reflecting the offence’s severity.
56.chapter: Chapter IV: Of Abetment, Criminal Conspiracy and Attempt

57.title: Abetting Commission of Offence by the Public or by More Than Ten Persons
57.text: Imposes severe punishment for abetting offences by large groups or the public, recognizing the heightened danger of collective criminality.
57.chapter: Chapter IV: Of Abetment, Criminal Conspiracy and Attempt

58.title: Concealing Design to Commit Offence Punishable With Death or Imprisonment for Life
58.text: Punishes concealing plans to commit serious offences, including through modern means like encryption, with varying penalties based on whether the offence is committed.
58.chapter: Chapter IV: Of Abetment, Criminal Conspiracy and Attempt

59.title: Public Servant Concealing Design to Commit Offence Which It Is His Duty to Prevent
59.text: Imposes stricter penalties on public servants who conceal designs to commit offences they are duty-bound to prevent, with penalties scaled by the offence’s commission.
59.chapter: Chapter IV: Of Abetment, Criminal Conspiracy and Attempt

60.title: Concealing Design to Commit Offence Punishable With Imprisonment
60.text: Punishes concealing plans to commit offences punishable with imprisonment, with penalties proportional to whether the offence is committed, to deter facilitation.
60.chapter: Chapter IV: Of Abetment, Criminal Conspiracy and Attempt

61.title: Criminal Conspiracy
61.text: Defines criminal conspiracy as an agreement to commit illegal acts or legal acts by illegal means, with punishments varying by the severity of the conspired offence.
61.chapter: Chapter IV: Of Abetment, Criminal Conspiracy and Attempt

62.title: Attempt to Commit Offences
62.text: Punishes attempts to commit offences with up to half the punishment for the completed offence, provided an act towards commission is done, to deter incomplete criminal acts.
62.chapter: Chapter IV: Of Abetment, Criminal Conspiracy and Attempt

63.title: Rape
63.text: Defines rape as non-consensual sexual penetration or manipulation under specific circumstances, including lack of consent, coercion, or incapacity, with exceptions for marital relations above a certain age.
63.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

64.title: Punishment for Rape
64.text: Prescribes punishment for rape, with enhanced penalties for aggravated cases involving authority figures, vulnerable victims, or severe circumstances, emphasizing deterrence and protection.
64.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

65.title: Punishment for Rape on Woman Under Sixteen Years of Age
65.text: Imposes severe punishment for rape on girls under sixteen, with mandatory minimum imprisonment and fines to support victim recovery, emphasizing child protection.
65.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

66.title: Punishment for Causing Death or Resulting in Persistent Vegetative State of Victim
66.text: Provides severe punishment, including potential death penalty, for rape resulting in the victim’s death or persistent vegetative state, reflecting the gravity of such outcomes.
66.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

67.title: Sexual Intercourse by Husband Upon His Wife During Separation or by a Person in Authority
67.text: Punishes non-consensual sexual intercourse by a husband during separation or by a person misusing authority, addressing abuse of power or trust.
67.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

68.title: Sexual Intercourse by a Person in Authority
68.text: Punishes sexual intercourse induced by abusing positions of authority or trust, short of rape, to protect women from exploitation.
68.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

69.title: Sexual Intercourse by Employing Deceitful Means, etc.
69.text: Punishes sexual intercourse induced by deceit, such as false promises of marriage or employment, to protect women from manipulation.
69.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

70.title: Gang Rape
70.text: Imposes severe punishment for gang rape, with enhanced penalties for cases involving minors, including potential death penalty, to deter collective sexual violence.
70.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

71.title: Punishment for Repeat Offenders
71.text: Enhances punishment for repeat offenders of serious sexual offences, prescribing life imprisonment or death to deter recidivism.
71.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

72.title: Disclosure of Identity of Victim of Certain Offences, etc.
72.text: Prohibits unauthorized disclosure of a victim’s identity in sexual offence cases, with exceptions for investigative or victim-authorized purposes, to protect privacy.
72.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

73.title: Printing or publishing any matter relating to Court proceedings without permission.
73.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

74.title: Assault or use of criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty
74.text: Punishes assault or criminal force against a woman with the intent to violate her modesty, ensuring protection of dignity.
74.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

75.title: Sexual harassment
75.text: Addresses various forms of sexual harassment, including physical advances, demands for favours, and inappropriate remarks, with tiered punishments.
75.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

76.title: Assault or use of criminal force to woman with intent to disrobe
76.text: Punishes assault or criminal force intended to disrobe a woman, protecting her dignity and safety.
76.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

77.title: Voyeurism
77.text: Penalizes voyeurism, including capturing or disseminating private images of a woman without consent, with increased penalties for repeat offenders.
77.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

78.title: Stalking
78.text: Addresses repeated unwanted contact or monitoring of a woman, with exceptions for lawful or justified conduct, and harsher penalties for repeat offenders.
78.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

79.title: Word, gesture or act intended to insult modesty of a woman
79.text: Punishes actions, words, or gestures intended to insult a woman’s modesty, including privacy violations.
79.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

80.title: Dowry death
80.text: Penalizes causing a woman’s death due to dowry-related cruelty or harassment, with a presumption of guilt for the husband or relatives.
80.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

81.title: Cohabitation caused by man deceitfully inducing belief of lawful marriage
81.text: Punishes men who deceive women into cohabitation by falsely inducing belief in a lawful marriage.
81.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

82.title: Marrying again during lifetime of husband or wife
82.text: Penalizes bigamy, with exceptions for cases where a prior marriage is void or the spouse has been absent for seven years.
82.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

83.title: Marriage ceremony fraudulently gone through without lawful marriage
83.text: Punishes fraudulent marriage ceremonies conducted with dishonest intent, where no lawful marriage occurs.
83.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

84.title: Enticing or taking away or detaining with criminal intent a married woman
84.text: Penalizes enticing or detaining a married woman with the intent of facilitating illicit intercourse.
84.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

85.title: Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty
85.text: Punishes cruelty by a husband or his relatives against a woman, protecting her from domestic abuse.
85.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

86.title: Cruelty defined
86.text: Defines cruelty as willful conduct or harassment causing harm or coercion, supporting Section 85’s provisions.
86.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

87.title: Kidnapping, abducting or inducing woman to compel her marriage, etc.
87.text: Punishes kidnapping or abduction of a woman to force her into marriage or illicit intercourse.
87.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

88.title: Causing miscarriage
88.text: Penalizes causing miscarriage without good faith, with harsher penalties if the woman is quick with child.
88.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

89.title: Causing miscarriage without woman’s consent
89.text: Imposes severe penalties for causing miscarriage without the woman’s consent, enhancing punishment for non-consensual acts.
89.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

90.title: Death caused by act done with intent to cause miscarriage
90.text: Punishes acts intended to cause miscarriage that result in the woman’s death, with mandatory life imprisonment if non-consensual.
90.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

91.title: Act done with intent to prevent child being born alive or to cause to die after birth
91.text: Penalizes acts intended to prevent a child from being born alive or causing its death after birth, unless done to save the mother’s life.
91.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

92.title: Causing death of quick unborn child by act amounting to culpable homicide
92.text: Punishes acts causing the death of a quick unborn child under circumstances amounting to culpable homicide.
92.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

93.title: Exposure and abandonment of child under twelve years of age, by parent or person having care of it
93.text: Penalizes parents or caregivers who abandon children under twelve with intent to wholly abandon them, with provisions for more severe charges if the child dies.
93.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

94.title: Concealment of birth by secret disposal of dead body
94.text: Punishes intentional concealment of a child’s birth through secret disposal of its body, regardless of when the child died.
94.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

95.title: Hiring, employing or engaging a child to commit an offence
95.text: Penalizes hiring or engaging children to commit offences, with harsher penalties for serious crimes.
95.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

96.title: Procuration of child
96.text: Punishes inducing a child for illicit intercourse, targeting exploitation and trafficking.
96.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

97.title: Kidnapping or abducting child under ten years of age with intent to steal from its person
97.text: Penalizes kidnapping or abducting a young child to steal from them, protecting vulnerable children.
97.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

98.title: Selling child for purposes of prostitution, etc.
98.text: Punishes selling or disposing of children for prostitution or immoral purposes, with a presumption of intent in certain cases, to combat child trafficking.
98.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

99.title: Buying child for purposes of prostitution, etc.
99.text: Punishes buying or obtaining children for prostitution or immoral purposes, with a presumption of intent in certain cases, to combat child trafficking and exploitation.
99.chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children

100.title: Culpable homicide
100.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

101.title: Murder
101.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

102.title: Culpable homicide by causing death of person other than person whose death was intended
102.text: Addresses situations where death is caused to an unintended victim, holding the offender liable as if the intended victim was killed.
102.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

103.title: Punishment for murder
103.text: Prescribes severe penalties for murder, reflecting its gravity as an offence against human life.
103.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

104.title: Punishment for murder by life-convict
104.text: Imposes harsher penalties for murder committed by a life convict, emphasizing deterrence for repeat offenders.
104.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

105.title: Punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder
105.text: Provides punishment for culpable homicide not classified as murder, with varying penalties based on intent.
105.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

106.title: Causing death by negligence
106.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

107.title: Abetment of suicide of child or person of unsound mind
107.text: Targets abetment of suicide for vulnerable individuals, imposing severe penalties to protect children and those with mental incapacities.
107.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

108.title: Abetment of suicide
108.text: Penalizes abetment of suicide generally, with imprisonment and fines to deter encouragement of such acts.
108.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

109.title: Attempt to murder
109.text: Penalizes attempts to commit murder with severe punishments, including imprisonment or death if hurt is caused, especially for those already under life imprisonment.
109.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

110.title: Attempt to commit culpable homicide
110.text: Penalizes attempts to commit culpable homicide not amounting to murder, with increased punishment if hurt is caused.
110.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

111.title: Organised crime
111.text: Addresses organised crime involving unlawful activities by syndicates or gangs, with severe penalties including death or life imprisonment for causing death, and substantial fines.
111.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

112.title: Petty organised crime
112.text: Penalizes petty organised crimes like theft, snatching, or illegal gambling by groups or gangs, with imprisonment and fines.
112.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

113.title: Terrorist act
113.text: Penalizes terrorist acts threatening India’s unity, integrity, or security, with severe penalties including death or life imprisonment for causing death, and fines.
113.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

114.title: Hurt
114.text: Defines the act of causing hurt as inflicting bodily pain, disease, or infirmity.
114.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

115.title: Voluntarily causing hurt
115.text: Penalizes the intentional or knowing act of causing hurt, with imprisonment or fines.
115.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

116.title: Grievous hurt
116.text: Defines grievous hurt as specific severe injuries, such as emasculation or permanent disfigurement.
116.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

117.title: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt
117.text: Penalizes the intentional or knowing act of causing grievous hurt, with imprisonment and fines.
117.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

118.title: Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means
118.text: Penalizes causing hurt or grievous hurt using dangerous weapons or means, with severe penalties including life imprisonment.
118.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

119.title: Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to extort property, or to constrain to an illegal act
119.text: Penalizes causing hurt or grievous hurt to extort property or constrain illegal acts, with severe penalties.
119.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

120.title: Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to extort confession, or to compel restoration of property
120.text: Penalizes causing hurt or grievous hurt to extort confessions or compel property restoration, with imprisonment and fines.
120.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

121.title: Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to deter public servant from his duty
121.text: Penalizes causing hurt or grievous hurt to deter public servants from their duties, with imprisonment and fines.
121.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

122.title: Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt on provocation
122.text: Penalizes causing hurt or grievous hurt due to grave and sudden provocation, with reduced penalties if not intended for others.
122.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

123.title: Causing hurt by means of poison, etc., with intent to commit an offence
123.text: Penalizes causing hurt using poison or drugs with intent to commit an offence, with imprisonment and fines.
123.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

124.title: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt by use of acid, etc.
124.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

125.title: Act endangering life or personal safety of others
125.text: Penalizes rash or negligent acts endangering life or safety, with increased penalties if hurt or grievous hurt is caused.
125.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

126.title: Wrongful restraint
126.text: Defines and penalizes wrongful restraint as obstructing a person’s lawful movement, with imprisonment or fines.
126.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

127.title: Wrongful confinement
127.text: Defines and penalizes wrongful confinement, with escalating penalties based on duration or intent, such as extortion or concealing confinement.
127.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

128.title: Force
128.text: Defines the use of force as causing motion or contact through bodily power, substances, or animals.
128.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

129.title: Criminal force
129.text: Defines and penalizes criminal force as intentional use of force without consent to commit an offence or cause injury, fear, or annoyance.
129.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

130.title: Assault
130.text: Defines assault as gestures or preparations causing apprehension of criminal force, with words potentially enhancing the act.
130.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

131.title: Punishment for assault or criminal force otherwise than on grave provocation
131.text: Penalizes assault or criminal force without grave provocation, with imprisonment or fines.
131.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

132.title: Assault or criminal force to deter public servant from discharge of his duty
132.text: Penalizes assault or criminal force to deter public servants from their duties, with imprisonment or fines.
132.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

133.title: Assault or criminal force with intent to dishonour person, otherwise than on grave provocation
133.text: Penalizes assault or criminal force intended to dishonour a person, without grave provocation, with imprisonment or fines.
133.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

134.title: Assault or criminal force in attempt to commit theft of property carried by a person
134.text: Penalizes assault or criminal force in attempting theft of property carried by a person, with imprisonment or fines.
134.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

135.title: Assault or criminal force in attempt to wrongfully confine a person
135.text: Penalizes assault or criminal force in attempting wrongful confinement, with imprisonment or fines.
135.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

136.title: Assault or criminal force on grave provocation
136.text: Penalizes assault or criminal force due to grave and sudden provocation, with reduced penalties.
136.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

137.title: Kidnapping
137.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

138.title: Abduction
138.text: Defines abduction as forcibly or deceitfully compelling a person to leave a place with intent to subject them to an offence.
138.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

139.title: Kidnapping or maiming a child for purposes of begging
139.text: Penalizes kidnapping or maiming a child for begging, with severe penalties including life imprisonment.
139.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

140.title: Kidnapping or abducting in order to murder or for ransom, etc.
140.text: Penalizes kidnapping or abduction with intent to murder, for ransom, or other offences, with life imprisonment or rigorous imprisonment.
140.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

141.title: Importation of girl or boy from foreign country
141.text: Penalizes importing minors into India for illicit intercourse or other offences, with imprisonment and fines.
141.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

142.title: Wrongfully concealing or keeping in confinement, kidnapped or abducted person
142.text: Penalizes concealing or confining a kidnapped or abducted person, with imprisonment and fines.
142.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

143.title: Trafficking of person
143.text: Penalizes trafficking of persons for exploitation, with severe penalties including life imprisonment for trafficking children or multiple persons, and fines.
143.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

144.title: Exploitation of a trafficked person
144.text: Penalizes the exploitation of trafficked persons or children, with rigorous imprisonment and fines, with higher penalties for exploiting trafficked children.
144.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

145.title: Habitual dealing in slaves
145.text: Penalizes habitual dealing in slaves with life imprisonment or up to ten years of imprisonment, along with fines.
145.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

146.title: Unlawful compulsory labour
146.text: Penalizes unlawful compulsory labour, compelling a person to work against their will, with imprisonment or fines.
146.chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Against the State

147.title: Waging, or attempting to wage war, or abetting waging of war, against the Government of India
147.text: Penalizes waging, attempting, or abetting war against the Government of India with death or life imprisonment and fines.
147.chapter: Chapter VII: Of Offences Against the State

148.title: Conspiracy to commit offences punishable by section 147
148.text: Penalizes conspiracy to wage war or overawe the government with criminal force, with life imprisonment or up to seven years and fines.
148.chapter: Chapter VII: Of Offences Against the State

149.title: Collecting arms, etc., with intention of waging war against the Government of India
149.text: Penalizes collecting arms or preparing to wage war against the Government of India with life imprisonment or up to ten years and fines.
149.chapter: Chapter VII: Of Offences Against the State

150.title: Concealing with intent to facilitate design to wage war
150.text: Penalizes concealing designs to wage war against the Government of India with up to seven years of imprisonment and fines.
150.chapter: Chapter VII: Of Offences Against the State

151.title: Assaulting President, Governor, etc., with intent to compel or restrain the exercise of any lawful power
151.text: Penalizes assaulting or restraining the President or Governor to influence their lawful powers with up to seven years of imprisonment and fines.
151.chapter: Chapter VII: Of Offences Against the State

152.title: Act endangering sovereignty, unity and integrity of India
152.text: Penalizes acts endangering India’s sovereignty, unity, or integrity, including exciting secession or rebellion, with life imprisonment or up to seven years and fines.
152.chapter: Chapter VII: Of Offences Against the State

153.title: Waging war against Government of any foreign State at peace with Government of India
153.chapter: Chapter VII: Of Offences Against the State

154.title: Committing depredation on territories of foreign State at peace with Government of India
154.chapter: Chapter VII: Of Offences Against the State

155.title: Receiving property taken by war or depredation mentioned in sections 153 and 154
155.chapter: Chapter VII: Of Offences Against the State

156.title: Public servant voluntarily allowing prisoner of State or war to escape
156.chapter: Chapter VII: Of Offences Against the State

157.title: Public servant negligently suffering such prisoner to escape
157.chapter: Chapter VII: Of Offences Against the State

158.title: Aiding escape of, rescuing or harbouring such prisoner.
158.text: A State prisoner or prisoner of war, who is permitted to be at large on his parole within certain limits in India, is said to escape from lawful custody if he goes beyond the limits within which he is allowed to be at large. Chapter VIII: Of Offences Relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force Description : Addresses offences that undermine the discipline, loyalty, and operational integrity of the Army, Navy, and Air Force, including abetting desertion, harbouring deserters, and acts of violence against military personnel.
158.chapter: Chapter VII: Of Offences Against the State

159.title: Abetting mutiny, or attempting to seduce a soldier, sailor or airman from his duty
159.text: Penalizes abetting mutiny or attempting to seduce military personnel from their allegiance or duty with life imprisonment or up to seven years and fines.
159.chapter: Chapter VIII: Of Offences Relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force

160.title: Abetment of mutiny, if mutiny is committed in consequence thereof
160.text: Penalizes abetment of mutiny resulting in actual mutiny with death, life imprisonment, or up to seven years and fines.
160.chapter: Chapter VIII: Of Offences Relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force

161.title: Abetment of assault by soldier, sailor or airman on his superior officer, when in execution of his office
161.text: Penalizes abetment of assault by military personnel on a superior officer during duty with up to three years of imprisonment and fines.
161.chapter: Chapter VIII: Of Offences Relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force

162.title: Abetment of such assault, if the assault is committed
162.text: Penalizes abetment of assault by military personnel on a superior officer, if the assault occurs, with up to seven years of imprisonment and fines.
162.chapter: Chapter VIII: Of Offences Relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force

163.title: Abetment of desertion of soldier, sailor or airman
163.text: Penalizes abetment of desertion by military personnel with up to two years of imprisonment, fines, or both.
163.chapter: Chapter VIII: Of Offences Relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force

164.title: Harbouring deserter
164.text: Penalizes harbouring a known deserter from the military with up to two years of imprisonment, fines, or both, except when harboured by the deserter’s spouse.
164.chapter: Chapter VIII: Of Offences Relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force

165.title: Deserter concealed on board merchant vessel through negligence of master
165.text: Penalizes the master of a merchant vessel for negligently allowing a military deserter to be concealed on board with a fine up to three thousand rupees.
165.chapter: Chapter VIII: Of Offences Relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force

166.title: Abetment of act of insubordination by soldier, sailor or airman
166.text: Penalizes abetment of known insubordination by military personnel, if insubordination occurs, with up to six months of imprisonment, fines, or both.
166.chapter: Chapter VIII: Of Offences Relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force

167.title: Persons subject to certain Acts
167.chapter: Chapter VIII: Of Offences Relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force

168.title: Wearing garb or carrying token used by soldier, sailor or airman
168.text: Penalizes non-military persons for wearing military garb or tokens to impersonate military personnel with up to three months of imprisonment, fines, or both.
168.chapter: Chapter VIII: Of Offences Relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force

169.title: Candidate, electoral right defined
169.text: Defines key terms for the chapter, specifying that a candidate is a nominated individual at an election and an electoral right includes the rights to candidacy, voting, or abstaining.
169.chapter: Chapter IX: Of Offences Relating to Elections

170.title: Bribery
170.text: Defines bribery as giving or accepting gratification to influence or reward the exercise of electoral rights, with provisions clarifying that public policy declarations are not offences.
170.chapter: Chapter IX: Of Offences Relating to Elections

171.title: Undue influence at elections
171.text: Penalizes interference with the free exercise of electoral rights through threats or inducements, with exceptions for public policy declarations or legal rights exercised without intent to interfere.
171.chapter: Chapter IX: Of Offences Relating to Elections

172.title: Personation at elections
172.text: Penalizes voting or applying for a voting paper in another’s name, a fictitious name, or multiple times, with an exception for authorized proxy voting.
172.chapter: Chapter IX: Of Offences Relating to Elections

173.title: Punishment for bribery
173.text: Specifies punishment for bribery with up to one year of imprisonment, fines, or both, with bribery by treating (e.g., providing food or entertainment) punishable by fine only.
173.chapter: Chapter IX: Of Offences Relating to Elections

174.title: Punishment for undue influence or personation at an election
174.text: Specifies punishment for undue influence or personation at an election with up to one year of imprisonment, fines, or both.
174.chapter: Chapter IX: Of Offences Relating to Elections

175.title: False statement in connection with an election
175.text: Penalizes making or publishing false statements about a candidate’s personal character or conduct to affect election results, punishable with a fine.
175.chapter: Chapter IX: Of Offences Relating to Elections

176.title: Illegal payments in connection with an election
176.text: Penalizes unauthorized election-related expenses without a candidate’s written authority, with fines up to ten thousand rupees, with a provision for post-facto approval for small expenses.
176.chapter: Chapter IX: Of Offences Relating to Elections

177.title: Failure to keep election accounts
177.text: Penalizes failure to maintain required election expense accounts, with fines up to five thousand rupees.
177.chapter: Chapter IX: Of Offences Relating to Elections

178.title: Counterfeiting coin, government stamps, currency-notes or bank-notes
178.chapter: Chapter X: Offences Relating to Coin, Currency-Notes, Bank-Notes, and Government Stamps

179.title: Using as genuine, forged or counterfeit coin, Government stamp, currency-notes or bank-notes
179.text: Penalizes using, importing, exporting, selling, or delivering forged or counterfeit coins, government stamps, currency-notes, or bank-notes as genuine, with imprisonment for life or up to seven years and fines.
179.chapter: Chapter X: Offences Relating to Coin, Currency-Notes, Bank-Notes, and Government Stamps

182.title: Making or using documents resembling currency-notes or bank-notes
182.text: Penalizes making or using documents resembling currency-notes or bank-notes, with fines up to three hundred rupees, and includes provisions for non-disclosure penalties and presumptions of responsibility.

1.text: In this section, "tribal areas" means the territories which immediately before the 21st day of January, 1972, were included in the tribal areas of Assam, as referred to in paragraph 20 of the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution, other than those within the local limits of the municipality of Shillong.

2.title: Definitions
2.text: Provides definitions to standardize terms used in criminal justice processes.

3.title: Construction of References
3.text: Ensures continuity in legal references post-repeal of the CrPC.

4.title: Trial of Offences under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 and Other Laws
4.text: Establishes that BNSS governs the procedure for offences under BNS and other laws, unless specified otherwise.

5.title: Saving
5.text: Preserves the applicability of special or local laws unless explicitly overridden by BNSS.

6.title: Classes of Criminal Courts
6.text: Defines the primary classes of criminal courts in addition to High Courts and special courts.
6.chapter: Chapter II: Constitution of Criminal Courts and Offices (Sections 6-20)

7.title: Territorial Divisions
7.text: Organizes the State into sessions divisions and districts for judicial administration.

9.text: Establishes Courts of Judicial Magistrates for districts outside metropolitan areas.

10.text: Outlines the roles and powers of Chief Judicial Magistrates and their deputies.

12.chapter: Chapter II: Constitution of Criminal Courts and Offices (Sections 6-20)

13.title: Subordination of Judicial Magistrates

14.chapter: Chapter II: Constitution of Criminal Courts and Offices (Sections 6-20)

16.text: Allows for the appointment of Special Metropolitan Magistrates for specific cases or classes of cases.

17.title: Subordination of Executive Magistrates
17.text: Establishes the hierarchy and control structure for Metropolitan Magistrates.
17.chapter: Chapter II: Constitution of Criminal Courts and Offices (Sections 6-20)

18.title: Public Prosecutors
18.text: Outlines the appointment process, eligibility criteria (minimum seven years of advocacy practice), and roles of Public Prosecutors and Additional Public Prosecutors, including provisions for Special Public Prosecutors and cadre-based appointments.
18.chapter: Chapter II: Constitution of Criminal Courts and Offices (Sections 6-20)

19.title: Assistant Public Prosecutors
19.text: Details the appointment of Assistant Public Prosecutors by the State or Central Government for magistrate court prosecutions, with provisions for the District Magistrate to appoint alternatives under specific conditions, excluding certain police officers.
19.chapter: Chapter II: Constitution of Criminal Courts and Offices (Sections 6-20)

20.title: Directorate of Prosecution
20.chapter: Chapter II: Constitution of Criminal Courts and Offices (Sections 6-20)

21.title: Courts by which offences are triable
21.text: Defines which courts (High Court, Court of Session, or others listed in the First Schedule) can try offences under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, or other laws, with a preference for women-presided courts for specific offences.

22.title: Sentences which High Courts and Sessions Judges may pass
22.text: Specifies the sentencing powers of High Courts (any sentence), Sessions/Additional Sessions Judges (any sentence, with death sentences needing High Court confirmation), and Assistant Sessions Judges (limited to sentences excluding death, life imprisonment, or terms over ten years).

24.title: Sentence of imprisonment in default of fine
24.text: Authorizes courts to impose additional imprisonment (up to one-fourth of the maximum imprisonment for the offence) in default of fine payment, to be served in addition to any imprisonment already sentenced.

25.title: Sentence in cases of conviction of several offences at one trial
25.text: Allows courts to impose concurrent or consecutive sentences for multiple offences in one trial, with limits on aggregate imprisonment (not exceeding 14 years or twice the court’s single-offence sentencing power) and treats consecutive sentences as a single sentence for appeal purposes.

26.title: Mode of conferring powers
26.text: Specifies that the High Court or State Government can confer powers under the BNSS by naming individuals, designating offices, or specifying classes of officials, with such powers effective upon communication to the empowered person.

27.title: Powers of officers appointed
27.text: Ensures that government officers vested with BNSS powers retain those powers when appointed to equal or higher offices in the same local area under the same State Government, unless the High Court or State Government directs otherwise.

28.title: Withdrawal of powers
28.text: Permits the High Court or State Government to withdraw powers conferred under the BNSS, and allows the Chief Judicial Magistrate or District Magistrate to withdraw powers they have conferred.

29.title: Powers of Judges and Magistrates exercisable by their successors-in-office
29.text: Allows successors-in-office to exercise the powers and duties of Judges or Magistrates, with the Chief Judicial Magistrate, District Magistrate, or Sessions Judge resolving any doubts about succession for Magistrates or Additional/Assistant Sessions Judges.

30.title: Powers of superior officers of police
30.text: Allows senior police officers to exercise the same powers as the officer in charge of a police station within their appointed local area, enhancing operational flexibility.
30.chapter: Chapter IV: Powers of Superior Officers of Police and Aid to the Magistrates and the Police (Sections 30-34)

31.title: Public when to assist Magistrates and police
31.text: Mandates public assistance to Magistrates or police in arresting authorized persons, preventing escapes, suppressing breaches of peace, or protecting public infrastructure like railways or telegraphs.
31.chapter: Chapter IV: Powers of Superior Officers of Police and Aid to the Magistrates and the Police (Sections 30-34)

32.title: Aid to person, other than police officer, executing warrant
32.text: Permits individuals to assist non-police warrant executors (e.g., court officers) in executing a warrant, provided the designated executor is present and actively executing it.
32.chapter: Chapter IV: Powers of Superior Officers of Police and Aid to the Magistrates and the Police (Sections 30-34)

33.title: Public to give information of certain offences
33.text: Obliges individuals to report knowledge of specific serious offences (e.g., murder, kidnapping, robbery, counterfeiting) or their intended commission under listed BNS sections to a Magistrate or police officer, unless they have a reasonable excuse. Extends to extraterritorial acts that would be offences in India.
33.chapter: Chapter IV: Powers of Superior Officers of Police and Aid to the Magistrates and the Police (Sections 30-34)

34.title: Duty of officers employed in connection with affairs of a village to make certain report
34.text: Requires village officers and residents to report to the nearest Magistrate or police station information about stolen property receivers, suspected robbers or escaped convicts, non-bailable offences, suspicious deaths, or extraterritorial acts that would be serious offences in India, as well as matters specified by the District Magistrate. Defines “village,” “proclaimed offender,” and “village officers” for clarity.
34.chapter: Chapter IV: Powers of Superior Officers of Police and Aid to the Magistrates and the Police (Sections 30-34)

35.title: When police may arrest without warrant
35.text: Authorizes police to arrest without a warrant for cognizable offences committed in their presence, suspected offences with specific conditions, proclaimed offenders, or other listed scenarios, with reasons recorded for arrests or non-arrests. Limits restraint to what is necessary.

36.title: Procedure of arrest and duties of officer making arrest
36.text: Mandates that arresting police officers wear clear identification, prepare an attested arrest memorandum, and inform the arrested person of their right to have a relative or friend notified, unless the memorandum is countersigned.

37.title: Designated police officer
37.text: Requires State Governments to set up police control rooms, designate a senior police officer to oversee arrest information and compliance with Chapter V, and maintain an online portal for arrest details.

38.title: Right of arrested person to meet an advocate of his choice during interrogation
38.text: Grants arrested persons the right to consult an advocate of their choice during police interrogation, but not for the entire duration.

39.title: Arrest on refusal to give name and residence
39.text: Allows police to arrest someone for a non-cognizable offence if they refuse to provide or provide false name and residence details, with release on bond once details are verified, or forwarding to a Magistrate if verification fails within 24 hours.

40.title: Arrest by private person and procedure on such arrest
40.text: Permits private persons to arrest those committing non-bailable cognizable offences or proclaimed offenders in their presence, requiring immediate handover to police, with provisions for re-arrest or release based on offence type and identity verification.

41.title: Arrest by Magistrate
41.text: Empowers Magistrates to arrest or order arrests for offences committed in their presence or for persons they are authorized to issue warrants for, within their jurisdiction, with custody subject to bail provisions.

42.title: Protection of members of Armed Forces from arrest
42.text: Protects Armed Forces members from arrest for actions in official duties without Central Government consent, with State Governments able to extend similar protections to specified public order maintenance forces.

43.title: Arrest how made
43.text: Specifies that arrests involve physical touch or confinement unless the person submits, with special provisions for women (presumed submission, no touching unless by female officer). Allows necessary force for resistance, permits handcuffs for specific cases with recorded reasons, and prohibits causing death unless the offence carries death or life imprisonment.

44.title: Search of place entered by person sought to be arrested
44.text: Authorizes police or warrant holders to demand entry and search places where an arrestee is believed to be, with provisions to break open doors/windows if entry is denied, respecting privacy for women in secluded apartments. Allows breaking open doors for self-liberation during arrests.

45.title: Power to break open door and window for purposes of liberation
45.text: Permits authorized persons to break open doors or windows to free themselves or others detained while lawfully attempting an arrest.

46.title: No unnecessary restraint
46.text: Prohibits excessive restraint during arrest, limiting it to what is necessary to prevent escape.

47.title: Person arrested to be informed of grounds of arrest and of right to bail
47.text: Requires police to inform arrested persons of the reasons for their arrest and, for bailable offences, their right to bail and to arrange sureties.

48.title: Obligation of person making arrest to inform about arrest, etc., to relative or friend
48.text: Mandates informing a nominated relative or friend of an arrest and the detention location, displaying arrest details at the police station, recording notifications, and requiring Magistrates to verify compliance.

49.title: Search of arrested person
49.text: Allows police to search arrested persons in non-bailable cases or when bail is unavailable, securing articles with a receipt, and requires female searches to be conducted by females with decency.

50.title: Power to seize offensive weapons
50.text: Permits immediate seizure of offensive weapons from arrested persons, with delivery to the relevant Court or officer.

51.title: Examination of accused by medical practitioner at request of police officer
51.text: Authorizes medical examinations of arrested persons by registered practitioners at police request when evidence may be obtained, using necessary force, with female examinations conducted or supervised by female practitioners, and reports sent promptly to investigators.

52.title: Examination of person accused of rape by medical practitioner
52.text: Specifically governs medical examinations for rape or attempted rape suspects, detailing report contents (e.g., DNA material, injuries), requiring precise conclusions, timing, and prompt submission to investigators and Magistrates.

53.title: Examination of arrested person by medical officer
53.text: Mandates medical examination of all arrested persons by government medical officers or practitioners, with female examinations by female officers, recording injuries and their timing, and ensuring same-sex inspections for non-medical checks, with prompt report submission.

54.title: Identification of person arrested
54.text: Allows courts to order arrested persons to undergo identification procedures if needed for investigation, with special provisions for disabled identifiers and witnesses, ensuring supervision or audio-video recording.

55.title: Procedure when police officer deputes subordinate to arrest without warrant
55.text: Specifies the protocol for a police officer to authorize a subordinate to perform a warrantless arrest, ensuring legal oversight and adherence to the conditions for such arrests, such as those for cognizable offences.

56.title: Health and safety of arrested person
56.text: Ensures that arrested individuals are treated with care, with obligations on authorities to safeguard their physical well-being, including access to medical care during detention.

57.title: Person arrested to be taken before Magistrate or officer in charge of police station
57.text: Mandates swift presentation of an arrested person to a judicial or police authority to ensure legal oversight and prevent arbitrary detention.

58.title: Person arrested not to be detained more than twenty-four hours
58.text: Protects against prolonged detention by requiring that arrested persons be presented to a Magistrate within 24 hours, ensuring judicial oversight.

59.title: Police to report apprehensions
59.text: Requires police to document and report arrests to maintain accountability and facilitate judicial or administrative review.

60.title: Discharge of person apprehended
60.text: Allows for the discharge of individuals when evidence or legal grounds for continued detention are lacking, protecting against wrongful detention.

61.title: Power, on escape, to pursue and retake
61.text: Empowers authorities to chase and re-arrest individuals who escape from custody, ensuring the integrity of the legal process.

62.title: Arrest to be made strictly according to Sanhita
62.text: Ensures that arrests adhere to the legal framework outlined in the Sanhita, safeguarding procedural integrity and the rights of the arrested.

436.title: Reference to High Court
436.text: This section enables courts to seek High Court guidance on legal questions, particularly regarding the validity of laws, and allows discretionary reference for other legal issues, with provisions for managing the accused’s custody or bail during the reference.

437.title: Disposal of case according to decision of High Court
437.text: This section mandates that courts follow the High Court’s decision on referred questions and allows the High Court to allocate costs for the reference process.

438.title: Calling for records to exercise powers of revision
438.text: This section empowers the High Court and Sessions Judge to review records of inferior courts to ensure justice, suspend sentences or orders, and order further inquiries, except in cases of acquittal, while preventing duplicate applications.

439.title: Power to order inquiry
439.text: This section allows the High Court or Sessions Judge to order further inquiries into cases where a discharge or dismissal order was issued, ensuring thorough review of judicial decisions.

440.title: Sessions Judge’s powers of revision
440.text: This section grants the Sessions Judge revisional powers similar to those of the High Court for cases within their jurisdiction, ensuring finality of their decisions to prevent further revisions by the same party.

441.title: Power of Additional Sessions Judge
441.text: This section allows an Additional Sessions Judge to exercise the same revisional powers as a Sessions Judge for cases assigned to them, ensuring flexibility in judicial administration.

442.title: High Court’s powers of revision
442.text: This section outlines the High Court’s revisional powers, allowing it to exercise appellate powers, ensure fair hearings, and handle revision applications as appeals when justified, while prohibiting conversion of acquittals to convictions.

443.title: Power of High Court to withdraw or transfer revision cases
443.text: This section allows the High Court to consolidate or transfer revision applications to ensure consistent adjudication and efficient case management.

444.title: Option of Court to hear parties
444.text: This section clarifies that there is no inherent right to a hearing in revision proceedings, but courts may discretionarily allow parties to be heard.

445.title: High Court’s order to be certified to lower Court
445.text: This section ensures that the High Court or Sessions Judge’s revisional decisions are communicated to the lower court, which must comply and amend records as needed.

446.title: Power of Supreme Court to transfer cases and appeals
446.text: This section empowers the Supreme Court to transfer cases or appeals between High Courts or subordinate courts for justice, upon application by the Attorney-General or interested parties, with provisions for compensating frivolous applications.
446.chapter: Chapter XXXIII: Transfer of Criminal Cases (Sections 446–452)

447.title: Power of High Court to transfer cases and appeals
447.text: This section enables the High Court to transfer cases or appeals for fair trials, legal complexity, or convenience, with procedural safeguards like notice to the Public Prosecutor and compensation for frivolous applications.
447.chapter: Chapter XXXIII: Transfer of Criminal Cases (Sections 446–452)

448.title: Power of Sessions Judge to transfer cases and appeals
448.text: This section allows a Sessions Judge to transfer cases within their sessions division for justice, applying similar procedural rules as the High Court, with a cap on compensation for frivolous applications.

449.title: Withdrawal of cases and appeals by Sessions Judge

449.chapter: Chapter XXXIII: Transfer of Criminal Cases (Sections 446–452)

450.title: Withdrawal of cases by Judicial Magistrate

451.text: This section permits District and Sub-divisional Magistrates to assign or withdraw cases from subordinate Magistrates for disposal, ensuring administrative flexibility.

453.text: Directs the Court of Session to promptly execute the High Court’s order confirming a death sentence or other related orders by issuing a warrant or taking necessary steps.

455.title: Postponement of execution of sentence of death in case of appeal to Supreme Court

457.title: Power to appoint place of imprisonment
457.text: Empowers the State Government to designate imprisonment locations and allows courts to transfer prisoners between civil and criminal jails, with provisions for release or return based on civil procedure laws.
457.chapter: Chapter XXXIV: Execution, Suspension, Remission and Commutation of Sentences (Sections 453–477)

458.text: Details the procedure for executing life or term imprisonment sentences, including issuing warrants and transferring the accused to the designated jail, with special provisions for short-term confinement.

468.chapter: Chapter XXXIV: Execution, Suspension, Remission and Commutation of Sentences (Sections 453–477)

469.title: Saving
469.text: Ensures that sentencing rules for escaped or previously convicted offenders do not reduce their liability, and delays default imprisonment for fines until after substantive sentences are served.
469.chapter: Chapter XXXIV: Execution, Suspension, Remission and Commutation of Sentences (Sections 453–477)

470.title: Return of warrant on execution of sentence
470.text: Requires the officer executing a sentence to return the warrant to the issuing court with a certified endorsement of how the sentence was carried out.
470.chapter: Chapter XXXIV: Execution, Suspension, Remission and Commutation of Sentences (Sections 453–477)

471.title: Money ordered to be paid recoverable as a fine
471.text: Treats non-fine monetary orders under the BNSS as recoverable like fines, with modified suspension rules for compensation or cost orders.
471.chapter: Chapter XXXIV: Execution, Suspension, Remission and Commutation of Sentences (Sections 453–477)

472.title: Mercy petition in death sentence cases
472.text: Permits the appropriate Government to suspend or remit sentences, including directing mercy petitions in death sentence cases, with specific timelines for disposal and provisions for re-arrest if conditions are breached.
472.chapter: Chapter XXXIV: Execution, Suspension, Remission and Commutation of Sentences (Sections 453–477)

473.title: Power to suspend or remit sentences
473.text: Grants the appropriate Government authority to suspend or remit sentences with conditions, requiring judicial input and allowing cancellation if conditions are unmet, with specific rules for petition presentation.
473.chapter: Chapter XXXIV: Execution, Suspension, Remission and Commutation of Sentences (Sections 453–477)

474.title: Power to commute sentence
474.text: Authorizes the appropriate Government to commute various sentences (e.g., death to lesser punishment, life imprisonment to a term or fine) without the sentenced person’s consent.
474.chapter: Chapter XXXIV: Execution, Suspension, Remission and Commutation of Sentences (Sections 453–477)

475.title: Restriction on powers of remission or commutation in certain cases
475.text: Restricts remission or commutation for life imprisonment in serious cases, requiring at least 14 years of actual imprisonment before release.
475.chapter: Chapter XXXIV: Execution, Suspension, Remission and Commutation of Sentences (Sections 453–477)
